rounds.text: G R Infraprojects is currently trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic value, with a DCF analysis suggesting a margin of safety of 36.2% [E44, E45]. The market has priced the stock at a P/E of 7.59x and a P/B of 0.78x, both of which sit well below their respective sector benchmarks of 13.81x and 1.26x [E1, E2, E6, E7]. This valuation disconnect is particularly striking given that the company has achieved a 31% compounded sales growth in the trailing twelve months and is currently in a capex build-up phase, evidenced by a 59.6% increase in capital work in progress [E17, E39]. Institutional confidence is also shifting, as foreign and domestic institutional holdings have increased by 1.73 and 3.69 percentage points respectively since December 2023 [E41, E42]. Conceded: the company faces headwinds including negative operating cash flow, declining operating margins, and a poor three-year compounded profit growth of -17% [E20, E29, E34]. Despite these challenges, the company’s recent performance shows a strong turnaround with 53% year-over-year net profit growth, suggesting that current market sentiment is lagging behind the improving fundamentals [E67, E72].
